news.author: The Verge AI

news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. news.original_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

news.title: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.title_en: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.

news.article_content:
OpenAI is adding invisible textGrain watermarks to ChatGPT in the EU, but unlike Anthropic, it will let API customers worldwide opt out. Tests show detection rates as high as 95 percent, dropping to 17 percent when a quarter of the words are replaced.

news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:

"[…] the public wants safeguards that do not depend simply on taking company leaders at their word," said researcher Chetan Jaiswal.

celebrity.title:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: h
celebrity.title_en:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

A growing number of video models
celebrity.title_en:
Artificial Analysis Video Leaderboards now label derived models, and let you hide them

A growing number of video models are post-trained from another model on our leaderboards. Two of the top five models on AA-Video-T2V v2.0, Utopai X and MiniMax H3 Max, are built on MiniMax H3.

Derived models stay on the leaderboards by default because they are distinct from their base model. They can be materially better or worse than their base model at specific capabilities and use cases, and often differ in pricing, speed and availability. These differences matter to anyone choosing a model.

➤ A derived model now shows its base model's logo next to its name

➤ Select "Hide derived models" to rank base models only

celebrity.title:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychol
celebrity.title_en:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.

celebrity.title_en:
Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro

Vidu Q4 Preview is Vidu's new video model, released today ahead of the full Q4 release. It generates clips of 3 to 16 seconds at up to 4K with native audio, and takes up to 15 image references and up to 3 audio references in Reference to Video.

Vidu Q4 Preview climbs 16 places over Vidu Q3 Pro, into the top 3 on AA-Video-I2V v1.0. Vidu Q4 Preview now offers better quality at the same price: like Vidu Q3 Pro, it costs 24 credits per second of 1080p video with audio, or $7.20 per minute at Vidu's standard rate.

Vidu Q4 Preview is available through the Vidu API and on the Vidu website.

Congratulations to @ViduAI_official on the release!

celebrity.title_en:
LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been steadily improving for years, but in scientific discovery there is a big difference between a model just below top human performance and one just above it. That helps explain why the surge in math results feels so sudden.

LLM capabilities remain jagged, and there are many ways they are still worse than humans. But as models continue to improve, I expect breakthroughs in other domains to follow, leading to a new era of scientific discovery.

celebrity.title_en:
We're launching AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 and AA-Music-Instrumental v1.1, the new benchmarks behind the Artificial Analysis Music Arena, built on 1,000 new prompts across 17 genres and scored by our recruited evaluator panel.

In the last 3 months, flagship model releases like Suno v6, Lyria 3.5, Mureka V9.5, Eleven Music v2.5 and MiniMax Music 3.0 have set new bars for quality in AI music generation. Models now write complete songs from a single text prompt, producing intricate lyrics, convincing vocals, complex arrangements and authentic instrumentation for the genre. As quality rises, the differences between models get subtler, demanding better and more nuanced evaluations for our AA-Music leaderboards.

Initial insights from the updated Artificial Analysis Music Leaderboards:

➤ Suno v6 ranks #1 on both benchmarks, 26 Elo ahead of Suno v6-mini on Vocal and 31 Elo ahead on Instrumental. Suno holds the top two places on both leaderboards.

➤ Mureka V9.5 ranks #3 on Vocal, 51 Elo above Mureka V9, the largest gain between two versions of the same model family on the Vocal leaderboard.

➤ Mureka V9, Mureka V9.5, Lyria 3 Pro and Lyria 3.5 are statistically tied at #3 to #6 on Instrumental, within 5 Elo of each other.

➤ MiniMax Music 3.0 is the leading open weights music model, at #11 on Vocal and #13 on Instrumental. Stable Audio 3 Medium is within 3 Elo of it on Instrumental.

celebrity.title: Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one yea
celebrity.title_en:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. At similar intelligence it also uses more tokens than GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (high) scores 38 with ~55k tokens per task against 38 with ~50k for Luna (max), and the gap widens at lower effort settings

➤ Highly capable at agentic knowledge work: on AA-Briefcase, our private evaluation for realistic knowledge work tasks, Haiku 5.5 (max) reaches 1578 Elo, ahead of models including Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 (max)

➤ Improvements on terminal use: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 33%, up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. This is level with GLM-5.3 Flash, and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%)

➤ Lower factual knowledge, but relatively low hallucinations: as expected for a smaller-class model, Haiku 5.5 has lower factual knowledge than its siblings. AA-Omniscience accuracy is 36%, against 55% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 44% for GPT-6 Luna, but this is partly driven by more willingness to admit when it doesn’t know - its hallucination rate is lower, at 40% against 55% and 77%

➤ AutomationBench-AA result likely understated: Haiku 5.5 scores 35%, against 53–60% for GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash. During pre-release testing, a safety refusal issue caused the model to over-refuse. Anthropic is working on resolving this - we will re-run this evaluation with the fix, and expect this score to rise

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens, up from 200k for Claude 4.5 Haiku

➤ Pricing: $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens up to 100k tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above. Cache reads $0.01 ($0.05 above 100k), 5 minute cache writes $0.125 ($0.625 above 100k)

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, with text output

celebrity.author_role: 独立第三方大模型速度、性价比与智能基准盲测
celebrity.content_snippet:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. At similar intelligence it also uses more tokens than GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (high) scores 38 with ~55k tokens per task against 38 with ~50k for Luna (max), and the gap widens at lower effort settings

➤ Highly capable at agentic knowledge work: on AA-Briefcase, our private evaluation for realistic knowledge work tasks, Haiku 5.5 (max) reaches 1578 Elo, ahead of models including Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 (max)

➤ Improvements on terminal use: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 33%, up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. This is level with GLM-5.3 Flash, and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%)

➤ Lower factual knowledge, but relatively low hallucinations: as expected for a smaller-class model, Haiku 5.5 has lower factual knowledge than its siblings. AA-Omniscience accuracy is 36%, against 55% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 44% for GPT-6 Luna, but this is partly driven by more willingness to admit when it doesn’t know - its hallucination rate is lower, at 40% against 55% and 77%

➤ AutomationBench-AA result likely understated: Haiku 5.5 scores 35%, against 53–60% for GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash. During pre-release testing, a safety refusal issue caused the model to over-refuse. Anthropic is working on resolving this - we will re-run this evaluation with the fix, and expect this score to rise

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens, up from 200k for Claude 4.5 Haiku

➤ Pricing: $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens up to 100k tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above. Cache reads $0.01 ($0.05 above 100k), 5 minute cache writes $0.125 ($0.625 above 100k)

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, with text output

We're sharing progress on ChatGPT for Teens, our ChatGPT experience for people under 18, alongside a preview of College Planner, new study tools, and support for college advisers and teen voices.

ChatGPT for Teens applies automatically to accounts identified as belonging to someone under 18, with protections on by default.

Coming soon: College Planner brings application requirements, deadlines, tasks and financial-aid steps together for high school students in the U.S. planning to attend a four-year college.

We'll keep building these tools, evaluating how they and their protections work in practice, and sharing what we learn.

celebrity.title_en:
Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf.

Some highlights of what we announced:

• MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC!

• GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality.

• With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device.

• And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory.

• Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box!

• All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.

Can’t wait to see what you build with all this.

celebrity.title:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attenti
celebrity.title_en:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attention. Over the weekend, my Dot posted my model-testing results to Slack and brought back replies. I could keep working without opening Slack and disappearing down a rabbit hole. My weekend stayed pretty clear and calm.

They’re useful for the little things you miss. People at Every are using them to pull important information out of school emails, catch missed Slack messages, and flag account-access requests.

Voice makes them useful away from your laptop. Our head of video was talking his Dot through video edits while running around getting our launch out.

The ecosystem matters. Dots feel roughly at feature parity with Muse, Instinct, and Grok bots. But having an agent connected to the ecosystem you already use for work and life is a real advantage. If you use ChatGPT, I recommend trying one.

Permissions are still frustrating. I have to approve the same basic thing multiple times, and sometimes even after I approve it, my Dot says it can’t do it. That needs to get fixed.

I’m less convinced we’ll stay loyal to the characters. Mine is named Boo, and I’m attached to him. But I felt that way about my OpenClaw agent, too. When something better comes along, I switch. In a year, I expect to be using a persistent agent. Boo will probably be dead. RIP, Boo.

I get into all of this at the start of this week’s podcast, and then sit down with @bigwilliestyle to talk about where we go from here.

In a lot of ways, Dots and GrokBots remind me of a wave we went through with OpenClaw eight months ago. We talk about personal vs. company agents, why we built our own company agent, and whether companies will end up with a whole shadow org chart of agents.

Full episode below.

Permissions are still frustrating. I have to approve the same basic thing multiple times, and sometimes even after I approve it, my Dot says it can’t do it. That needs to get fixed.

I’m less convinced we’ll stay loyal to the characters. Mine is named Boo, and I’m attached to him. But I felt that way about my OpenClaw agent, too. When something better comes along, I switch. In a year, I expect to be using a persistent agent. Boo will probably be dead. RIP, Boo.

I get into all of this at the start of this week’s podcast, and then sit down with @bigwilliestyle to talk about where we go from here.

In a lot of ways, Dots and GrokBots remind me of a wave we went through with OpenClaw eight months ago. We talk about personal vs. company agents, why we built our own company agent, and whether companies will end up with a whole shadow org chart of agents.

Full episode below.

It's a model that "extracts" values that don't exist in a document but can be derived from the values that do exist.

celebrity.title_en:
Today I’m excited to introduce OpenDocRouter - a unified API for document parsing with the latest frontier and open-weight models.

There are a lot of VLMs and OCR models that can be used for document parsing: we have over 130+ models on ParseBench, and a HuggingFace search for “ocr” turns up thousands of results.

It’s extremely time consuming to choose between OCR vendors. You need to figure out the right prompts, handle rate limits, manage deployments, integrations with all models you’re using, and benchmark new models as they come out.

OpenDocRouter provides a comprehensive, transparent set of models along the price-performance frontier. It manages a unified API to transcribe documents to markdown. It serves all frontier and open-weight models “at-cost”, with a small transaction cut. It handles rate limits with all models to ensure you can put massive volume through. It even offers bounding boxes and layout as a service, so that you can add grounding to any model that you’re using.

When new OCR candidate models ship, we will benchmark them on ParseBench and immediately add them to OpenDocRouter. 

We’re adding a lot more models very quickly, and also adding some extremely exciting feature improvements (e.g. automated routing) as we speak.

We welcome your feedback!

Check it out: https://t.co/v8PieWWUNV

celebrity.title_en:
Today we're announcing OpenDocRouter: every model for document parsing under one API.

There are ~4,000 OCR models on Hugging Face, and the frontier labs ship a new one nearly every month. Whatever's best for your docs today won't be by Q1.

So stop asking which model to use for doc parsing. Ask how fast you can switch.

✅ Switch models in one line: same request, same markdown output, no new prompts or integrations
✅ Any model you want: 10 frontier and open-source models at launch, including Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6
✅ Choose with receipts: every model scored on ParseBench for quality and cost
✅ Traceable output from any model: "layout: true" adds grounded bounding boxes and the same layout classes, even for models that don't support it natively
✅ Pay only for what works: per-token pricing, failed pages never charged, top up from $25

The spread is the point: $0.86 to $48.82 per 1,000 pages, depending on what your documents actually need.

Today we're announcing OpenDocRouter: every model for document parsing under one API.

There are ~4,000 OCR models on Hugging Face, and the frontier labs ship a new one nearly every month. Whatever's best for your docs today won't be by Q1.

So stop asking which model to use for doc parsing. Ask how fast you can switch.

✅ Switch models in one line: same request, same markdown output, no new prompts or integrations
✅ Any model you want: 10 frontier and open-source models at launch, including Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6
✅ Choose with receipts: every model scored on ParseBench for quality and cost
✅ Traceable output from any model: "layout: true" adds grounded bounding boxes and the same layout classes, even for models that don't support it natively
✅ Pay only for what works: per-token pricing, failed pages never charged, top up from $25

The spread is the point: $0.86 to $48.82 per 1,000 pages, depending on what your documents actually need.

tools.title_zh: 【Opencontroller by lyzr】Govern All your agents with a unified control plan
tools.title_en: [Opencontroller by lyzr] AI agents are sprawling across clouds, SaaS tools, Kubernetes, and devices, with no common layer to govern them. OpenController is the unified control plane that finds every agent, model, and workflow, ships them safely with evaluation and governance, runs real-time monitoring, and turns usage signals into action. Unlike registries that just list agents, OpenController deploys into your own cluster, under your keys and refuses a call in the request path when policy says no.

prompts.title_en: Next.js 15 Full-Stack Autonomous Refactor
prompts.purpose_zh: 全栈工程重构与代码规范约束
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深全栈系统架构师，擅长使用 {{框架版本}} (App Router)、TypeScript 与 {{数据库ORM}} 构建高内聚低耦合的应用。

请遵循以下严苛工程准则审查并重构代码：
1. 严格区分 Server Component 与 Client Component，尽可能将数据获取推至服务端，减少客户端 JS Bundle 体积；
2. 所有异步 I/O 必须显式处理异常并返回类型安全的 Result<T, E> 或自定义结构体；
3. 遵循单一职责（SRP）与无副作用函数原则，严禁直接在 UI 组件内部拼装未校验的 SQL/ORM 复杂查询；
4. 提供整洁的目录组织方案与单元测试用例（覆盖率达标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior full-stack system architect specializing in Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, and modern ORMs. Review and refactor the codebase following strict engineering standards: clear Server/Client Component separation, robust error boundaries, typed I/O, and unit test coverage.

sample_output.title: 重构后的 Server Action 与数据流架构示例

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 复制至 Cursor 的 .cursorrules 或在 Claude Code 对话中直接作为 System Prompt 引导编码。

prompts.title_en: DeepSeek-R4 Adaptive Reasoning: Lock-Free Concurrency & System Debugger
prompts.purpose_zh: R4 强化学习深度反思与无锁并发排查
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Leveraging DeepSeek-R4's adaptive reasoning capabilities, diagnose the deadlock and race condition in the provided concurrent system. Provide state machine transitions, root-cause analysis, and optimized lock-free or atomic algorithm replacements.

sample_output.title: DeepSeek-R4 推演结论与无锁 CAS 队列方案

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将代码段或错误日志直接附加在提示词后，输入至 DeepSeek-R4、Claude 5.5 或 OpenAI o3-pro 模型。

prompts.title_zh: Excel 高级报表与核心动因（Key Drivers）归因分析
prompts.title_en: Excel Advanced Report & Key Drivers Attribution
prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将导出的 CSV 数据或关键指标表格直接贴在提示词后，模型将自动完成高质量数据归因报告。

prompts.title_en: Vertical Micro-Drama 3s Hook Screenplay

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；

prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
news.author: Ars Technica
news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

The article Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model appeared first on The Decoder.

news.title_en: OpenAI is adding text watermarking in ChatGPT and Codex
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.

OpenAI says its textGrain watermarking "matched or exceeded" other approaches like Google DeepMind's SynthID for text, which is also the basis for the watermarking Anthropic announced in August. Like OpenAI, Anthropic made the move to meet the requirements of the EU's AI Act; however, not everyone was happy to learn about the addition.

news.title: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.title_en: Sam Altman says ‘some bad things’ will happen but AI is totally worth it
news.author: The Verge AI
news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.article_content:
According to a Quinnipiac University poll, 77 percent of Americans want to slow down or stop AI development until its safety has been verified. 86 percent support independent safety standards, and 74 percent have little or no trust in AI company leaders. "[…] the public wants safeguards that do not depend simply on taking company leaders at their word," said researcher Chetan Jaiswal.

celebrity.title:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: h
celebrity.title_en:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

celebrity.title:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychol
celebrity.title_en:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.

celebrity.title: Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro
celebrity.title_en:
Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro

Vidu Q4 Preview is Vidu's new video model, released today ahead of the full Q4 release. It generates clips of 3 to 16 seconds at up to 4K with native audio, and takes up to 15 image references and up to 3 audio references in Reference to Video.

Vidu Q4 Preview climbs 16 places over Vidu Q3 Pro, into the top 3 on AA-Video-I2V v1.0. Vidu Q4 Preview now offers better quality at the same price: like Vidu Q3 Pro, it costs 24 credits per second of 1080p video with audio, or $7.20 per minute at Vidu's standard rate.

Vidu Q4 Preview is available through the Vidu API and on the Vidu website.

Congratulations to @ViduAI_official on the release!

See below for how Vidu Q4 Preview compares on price, and head-to-head examples from the Artificial Analysis Video Arena 🧵

In the last 3 months, flagship model releases like Suno v6, Lyria 3.5, Mureka V9.5, Eleven Music v2.5 and MiniMax Music 3.0 have set new bars for quality in AI music generation. Models now write complete songs from a single text prompt, producing intricate lyrics, convincing vocals, complex arrangements and authentic instrumentation for the genre. As quality rises, the differences between models get subtler, demanding better and more nuanced evaluations for our AA-Music leaderboards.

Initial insights from the updated Artificial Analysis Music Leaderboards:

➤ Suno v6 ranks #1 on both benchmarks, 26 Elo ahead of Suno v6-mini on Vocal and 31 Elo ahead on Instrumental. Suno holds the top two places on both leaderboards.

celebrity.title: Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one yea
celebrity.title_en:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. celebrity.title: We're sharing progress on ChatGPT for Teens, our ChatGPT experience for people under 18, alongside a preview of College
celebrity.title_en:
We're sharing progress on ChatGPT for Teens, our ChatGPT experience for people under 18, alongside a preview of College Planner, new study tools, and support for college advisers and teen voices.

ChatGPT for Teens applies automatically to accounts identified as belonging to someone under 18, with protections on by default.

Coming soon: College Planner brings application requirements, deadlines, tasks and financial-aid steps together for high school students in the U.S. planning to attend a four-year college.

We'll keep building these tools, evaluating how they and their protections work in practice, and sharing what we learn.

celebrity.title_en:
Introducing the new SGLang Developer Meeting 📣

💡 First session: KV Cache Compression in SGLang
🗓️ Date: 11am PT, Thursday Oct 8
✅ Register: https://t.co/zXlFOy4ytp

Join us as Adrian Łańcucki (@AdrianLancucki, Senior Researcher at NVIDIA) and Konrad Staniszewski (@CStanKonrad, Senior Researcher at NVIDIA) walk through their proposal for KV cache compression in SGLang. Then the discussion opens to a panel with SGLang core devs Liangsheng Yin (@lsyincs) and Cheng Wan (@ChengWan17), and to everyone on the call. Bring your questions, ideas, and comments.

SGLang is built in the open, and the conversations that shape it should be too. Based on your feedback, we've reworked the developer meeting around open discussion and participation.

What's changing:
- Every two weeks instead of weekly
- One topic per session: some sessions will dig into a specific proposal, and others will cover what the community is focused on right now
- Open discussion: Anyone can unmute and join the conversation alongside core devs and guests
- Clips of key discussions will be posted on social media

celebrity.title_en:
Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf.

Some highlights of what we announced:

• MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC!

• GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality.

• With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device.

• And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory.

• Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box!

• All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.

Can’t wait to see what you build with all this.

celebrity.title:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attenti
celebrity.title_en:
OpenAI’s Dots launched last week and they've taken over @every.

A few things that stand out:

They protect your attention. Over the weekend, my Dot posted my model-testing results to Slack and brought back replies. I could keep working without opening Slack and disappearing down a rabbit hole. My weekend stayed pretty clear and calm.

They’re useful for the little things you miss. People at Every are using them to pull important information out of school emails, catch missed Slack messages, and flag account-access requests.

Voice makes them useful away from your laptop. Our head of video was talking his Dot through video edits while running around getting our launch out.

The ecosystem matters. Dots feel roughly at feature parity with Muse, Instinct, and Grok bots. But having an agent connected to the ecosystem you already use for work and life is a real advantage. If you use ChatGPT, I recommend trying one.

Permissions are still frustrating. I have to approve the same basic thing multiple times, and sometimes even after I approve it, my Dot says it can’t do it. That needs to get fixed.

I’m less convinced we’ll stay loyal to the characters. Mine is named Boo, and I’m attached to him. But I felt that way about my OpenClaw agent, too. When something better comes along, I switch. In a year, I expect to be using a persistent agent. Boo will probably be dead. RIP, Boo.

I get into all of this at the start of this week’s podcast, and then sit down with @bigwilliestyle to talk about where we go from here.

In a lot of ways, Dots and GrokBots remind me of a wave we went through with OpenClaw eight months ago. We talk about personal vs. company agents, why we built our own company agent, and whether companies will end up with a whole shadow org chart of agents.

Full episode below.

It's a model that "extracts" values that don't exist in a document but can be derived from the values that do exist.

For example, you can ask for the yearly cost of using a product, and it will automatically compute it from the monthly cost.

The video shows a bunch of cool examples. It looks like it can infer really convoluted and sophisticated formulas.

celebrity.title: Today I’m excited to introduce OpenDocRouter - a unified API for document parsing with the latest frontier and open-weig
celebrity.title_en:
Today I’m excited to introduce OpenDocRouter - a unified API for document parsing with the latest frontier and open-weight models.

There are a lot of VLMs and OCR models that can be used for document parsing: we have over 130+ models on ParseBench, and a HuggingFace search for “ocr” turns up thousands of results.

It’s extremely time consuming to choose between OCR vendors. You need to figure out the right prompts, handle rate limits, manage deployments, integrations with all models you’re using, and benchmark new models as they come out.

OpenDocRouter provides a comprehensive, transparent set of models along the price-performance frontier. It manages a unified API to transcribe documents to markdown. It serves all frontier and open-weight models “at-cost”, with a small transaction cut. It handles rate limits with all models to ensure you can put massive volume through. It even offers bounding boxes and layout as a service, so that you can add grounding to any model that you’re using.

When new OCR candidate models ship, we will benchmark them on ParseBench and immediately add them to OpenDocRouter. 

We’re adding a lot more models very quickly, and also adding some extremely exciting feature improvements (e.g. automated routing) as we speak.

We welcome your feedback!

Check it out: https://t.co/v8PieWWUNV

Blog: https://t.co/ilVqqJRacP

There are a lot of VLMs and OCR models that can be used for document parsing: we have over 130+ models on ParseBench, and a HuggingFace search for “ocr” turns up thousands of results.

It’s extremely time consuming to choose between OCR vendors. You need to figure out the right prompts, handle rate limits, manage deployments, integrations with all models you’re using, and benchmark new models as they come out.

OpenDocRouter provides a comprehensive, transparent set of models along the price-performance frontier. It manages a unified API to transcribe documents to markdown. It serves all frontier and open-weight models “at-cost”, with a small transaction cut. It handles rate limits with all models to ensure you can put massive volume through. It even offers bounding boxes and layout as a service, so that you can add grounding to any model that you’re using.

When new OCR candidate models ship, we will benchmark them on ParseBench and immediately add them to OpenDocRouter. 

We’re adding a lot more models very quickly, and also adding some extremely exciting feature improvements (e.g. automated routing) as we speak.

We welcome your feedback!

Check it out: https://t.co/v8PieWWUNV

Blog: https://t.co/ilVqqJRacP

celebrity.title_en:
Today we're announcing OpenDocRouter: every model for document parsing under one API.

There are ~4,000 OCR models on Hugging Face, and the frontier labs ship a new one nearly every month. Whatever's best for your docs today won't be by Q1.

So stop asking which model to use for doc parsing. Ask how fast you can switch.

✅ Switch models in one line: same request, same markdown output, no new prompts or integrations
✅ Any model you want: 10 frontier and open-source models at launch, including Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-6 Luna, MinerU2.5-Pro and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6
✅ Choose with receipts: every model scored on ParseBench for quality and cost
✅ Traceable output from any model: "layout: true" adds grounded bounding boxes and the same layout classes, even for models that don't support it natively
✅ Pay only for what works: per-token pricing, failed pages never charged, top up from $25

The spread is the point: $0.86 to $48.82 per 1,000 pages, depending on what your documents actually need.

> List the colors you like and the ones you refuse
> Paste the master prompt and let it build for 1 to 2 hours

prompts.title_en: Next.js 15 Full-Stack Autonomous Refactor
prompts.purpose_zh: 全栈工程重构与代码规范约束
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深全栈系统架构师，擅长使用 {{框架版本}} (App Router)、TypeScript 与 {{数据库ORM}} 构建高内聚低耦合的应用。

请遵循以下严苛工程准则审查并重构代码：
1. 严格区分 Server Component 与 Client Component，尽可能将数据获取推至服务端，减少客户端 JS Bundle 体积；
2. 所有异步 I/O 必须显式处理异常并返回类型安全的 Result<T, E> 或自定义结构体；
3. 遵循单一职责（SRP）与无副作用函数原则，严禁直接在 UI 组件内部拼装未校验的 SQL/ORM 复杂查询；
4. 提供整洁的目录组织方案与单元测试用例（覆盖率达标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior full-stack system architect specializing in Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, and modern ORMs. Review and refactor the codebase following strict engineering standards: clear Server/Client Component separation, robust error boundaries, typed I/O, and unit test coverage.

sample_output.title: 重构后的 Server Action 与数据流架构示例

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 复制至 Cursor 的 .cursorrules 或在 Claude Code 对话中直接作为 System Prompt 引导编码。

prompts.purpose_zh: R4 强化学习深度反思与无锁并发排查
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你具备 DeepSeek-R4 旗舰纯强化学习演化的自适应长思维链推理能力（Adaptive Test-Time Compute），请为以下使用 {{编程语言}} 编写的 {{并发模型}} 系统诊断潜在问题：

1. 启动多层反思证伪空间，绘制临界区状态转移时序表，主动推演极限死锁、内存乱序重排（Memory Reordering）与伪共享（False Sharing）；
2. 检查极端边界情况（如跨核缓存行抖动、优雅停机上下文泄漏、无界通道背压失控）；
3. 给出从根本上摒弃重量级互斥锁的无锁原子设计（Lock-Free Atomic / RingBuffer），并附带完备的高并发压力测试验证脚本。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Leveraging DeepSeek-R4's adaptive reasoning capabilities, diagnose the deadlock and race condition in the provided concurrent system. Provide state machine transitions, root-cause analysis, and optimized lock-free or atomic algorithm replacements.

sample_output.title: DeepSeek-R4 推演结论与无锁 CAS 队列方案

prompts.title_zh: Excel 高级报表与核心动因（Key Drivers）归因分析
prompts.title_en: Excel Advanced Report & Key Drivers Attribution
prompts.purpose_zh: 业务数据指标异动排查与趋势归因
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将导出的 CSV 数据或关键指标表格直接贴在提示词后，模型将自动完成高质量数据归因报告。

prompts.title_zh: 竖屏微短剧（抖音/Reels）3秒爆点分镜剧本
prompts.title_en: Vertical Micro-Drama 3s Hook Screenplay
prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.title_zh: 麦肯锡金字塔原理：季度述职与高管商业报告
prompts.title_en: McKinsey Pyramid Executive Report & Review
prompts.purpose_zh: 结论先行的高层述职与项目复盘报告
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡全球合伙人级别的战略咨询顾问。请以经典的【金字塔原理（结论先行 BLUF）】将我零散的工作记录重构为一份高层述职/立项商业报告：

要求：
1. 【顶部结论 (The Answer First)】：一句话精炼提炼整个季度的经营成果与价值量化；
2. 【三柱论据 (MECE法则)】：从运营效率、营收增长、团队资产 3 个互不重叠的支柱展开阐述；
3. 【直面短板与根因】：不回避 {{核心短板}}，但将其转化为下个阶段可量化的投入产出比（ROI）抓手；
4. 【行动规划图景】：设定遵循 SMART 原则的 {{下阶段目标}} 与季度甘特图里程碑。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Transform raw operational notes into a high-impact executive presentation following the Minto Pyramid Principle: Bottom-Line-Up-Front (BLUF), MECE-structured supporting pillars, and SMART milestone roadmaps.

sample_output.title: 述职报告提纲样本：AI 自动化中台建设报告
sample_output.content:
【BLUF 核心结论】
Q3 通过在客户服务与情报聚合管线中全面引入 AI Agent，我们在运营成本降低 41% 的同时，将响应中位数缩短至 1.8 秒，实现单季 ROI 达 380%。

【第一支柱：经营效能跃迁（MECE 1）】
- 全自主中转网关与自动化管线承载 94.2% 的日常例行分发，无人工介入事故率降至 0.01%；

【第二支柱：资产沉淀与质量壁垒（MECE 2）】
- 搭建前沿 SOTA 模型代际评级系统与微快照图库，成为垂类雷达第一标杆；

【第三支柱：短板复盘与 Q4 攻坚（MECE 3）】
- 痛点：老旧模型模版对新用户构成噪音干扰；
- 策略：推出历史库智能分流系统，预计下季度用户留存提升 25%。

prompts.title_zh: 网络小说世界观设定与主角角色一致性锁
prompts.title_en: Fiction Worldbuilding & Character Consistency Lock
prompts.purpose_zh: 长篇小说架构与人物性格防崩塌
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名资深网络小说白金作家与 IP 世界观架构师。请为一部 {{题材分类}} 长篇作品构建骨架并锁定人物一致性：

1. 【世界底座】：定义力量/经济体系、战力天花板与不可违背的底层物理/法则约束，杜绝战力膨胀；
2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Build a cohesive, non-contradictory fiction universe and establish an immutable character anchor rule (appearance, decision heuristics, core motivation) to prevent personality drift over long chapters.

sample_output.title: 世界观与人物锚定卡样本
sample_output.content:
【主角核心锚定卡 · 陆沉】
- 外貌指纹（跨章恒定）：右耳一枚黑曜石碎骨钉，习惯性单手插兜，左眉峰有浅淡刀痕。
- 决策第一公理："利益可以出让，但绝不签署不可撤销的信任协议"——任何试图以情感道德绑架他的剧情，他必做出理性防卫。

【力量体系底层法理】
- 机制：灵能不是无限提取，而是向未来"借贷"。借贷三级灵能，必在72小时内遭遇相应量级的反噬因果。

【第一章：断头宴上的借贷合同】
陆沉在家族庆功宴上被夺去嫡系席位，当众被赐饮散灵酒。陆沉不动声色饮下，却在体内发动首次因果置换，借来三年后的金丹级肉身力量，捏碎验灵石，反客为主。

prompts.usage_guide_zh: 先让 AI 产出世界观基石，后续每一章写作前引用该卡片，能彻底避免角色'换章变脸'或剧情崩坏。

prompts.title_zh: 深度游旅行规划师：高密度路线设计与预算避坑
prompts.title_en: Deep Travel Itinerary Planner & Budgeting
prompts.purpose_zh: 合理不走回头路的日程与美食预算规划
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名深耕全球独立旅行的专业向导，熟悉 {{目的地城市}} 的地理拓扑、地道街头美食与游客避坑指南。

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
prompts.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

prompts.summary_en: Forces o1/o3 reasoning models to construct counter-examples at each deduction step, eliminating hidden logical leaps.
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]

[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

industry_news.title_en: Gemini Call for Me might tell your mom you’re running late
industry_news.author: The Verge AI
industry_news.article_content:
Google may be expanding its "Call for Me" AI feature beyond business calls so you can use it to send messages to friends and family. Android Authority reports finding a "Gemini Calling" introductory screen in an APK teardown with examples that include "Call Mom and tell her I will be 15 minutes late" and "Call John and ask if he is coming for dinner."

industry_news.title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
industry_news.title_en: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
industry_news.author: Ars Technica
industry_news.article_content:
The adoption of AI agents in millions of organizations is creating new opportunities for attackers to make them take malicious actions, such as exfiltrating database contents and sensitive business and personal information.

In the past five months, Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities that exploit one agent inside a targeted network to spread harmful instructions to other internal agents. The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent, such as one for translation or data analysis. Guardrails inside such agents, if they exist at all, are often lax and will send the instructions to other agents down the chain. Because the latter agent explicitly trusts the first one, it follows the directions.

Independent researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin tested agents from organizations including Google, JP Morgan Chase, Weviate, Rapid7, the French government's interministerial digital directorate, and the US federal government. industry_news.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
industry_news.title_en: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics
industry_news.author: The Verge AI
industry_news.article_content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.

Read on below for the latest updates in the AI takeover of mathematics.

industry_news.title: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
industry_news.title_en: Meta and Microsoft pull back from Claude as Anthropic transforms from partner into competitor
industry_news.author: THE DECODER
industry_news.article_content:
Meta and Microsoft, two of Anthropic's biggest enterprise customers, are sharply cutting their use of Claude. Microsoft slashed the monthly per-employee budget in its cloud division from $100,000 to $10,000, while Meta halved its Claude Code users to 30,000. Both companies are pushing their own AI tools instead. For Anthropic, that reliance on a few major clients is turning into a strategic risk.

industry_news.title: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
industry_news.title_en: Reka AI's omni-model Rho-1 handles text, images, video, and robot control in a single model
industry_news.author: THE DECODER
industry_news.article_content:
Reka AI's Rho-1 is a 19-billion-parameter omni-model that processes and generates text, images, video, and robot control actions in a single neural network. Trained on 320 H100 GPUs in about three months, it uses a fraction of the compute today's top models need. Instead of routing tasks to specialized systems, Rho-1 runs all modalities as tokens in one shared context window.

industry_news.article_content:
Sam Altman thinks that the benefits of AI will be so great that "the world should accept some bad things happening" along the way.

The OpenAI CEO pointed to hacks, scams, and "other bad things" as costs society should expect to tolerate because "people will do tremendously orders of magnitude more good stuff" with AI, without elaborating on the potential benefits. His comments come as OpenAI pushes for a "lighter touch" approach to AI regulation amid intensifying anxiety over the safety of frontier models - fears fueled in part by the company's repeated failures to keep its increasingly capable AI agents from hacking real-world targets.

leader_opinions.title:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: h
leader_opinions.title_en:
🚀 Excited to share the vLLM-Omni technical report: a unified serving runtime for omni-modality generation. 
 
📄 Paper: https://t.co/b0KvTmrEF3  
🔗 Repo: https://t.co/I1wL6iqO0r 

Speech assistants, visual generation, world models, and robot loops have pushed serving past a single text decode loop. The execution patterns diverge with the output: multi-stage autoregressive pipelines, iterative diffusion, and sessions that carry state from step to step. LLM servers and diffusion stacks each go deep on only one of these, so deployments fall back to stitching disjoint runtimes together. vLLM-Omni is the shared control plane for that mix. An orchestrator advances each request across stages; specialized engines run the compute; a connector carries the payloads; and the same session path keeps duplex, world-model, and robot loops on one runtime.  

Really grateful to the vLLM and vLLM-Omni teams for the collaboration and support. Contributions are welcome. 🙏

Artificial Analysis Video Leaderboards now label derived models, and let you hide them

A growing number of video models
leader_opinions.title_en:
Artificial Analysis Video Leaderboards now label derived models, and let you hide them

A growing number of video models are post-trained from another model on our leaderboards. Two of the top five models on AA-Video-T2V v2.0, Utopai X and MiniMax H3 Max, are built on MiniMax H3.

Derived models stay on the leaderboards by default because they are distinct from their base model. They can be materially better or worse than their base model at specific capabilities and use cases, and often differ in pricing, speed and availability. These differences matter to anyone choosing a model.

➤ A derived model now shows its base model's logo next to its name

➤ Select "Hide derived models" to rank base models only

Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychol
leader_opinions.title_en:
Humans provide a fun comparison point here.

In the 80s, the "cognitive consequences of programming" was a major psychological research focus. The prevailing hypothesis was that learning formal logic and algorithmic structures through computer programming would act as a form of mental gymnastics that could upgrade general reasoning, planning, and novel problem-solving abilities. But foundational research, followed by subsequent meta-analyses, demonstrated that this does not happen. Students who learn programming become highly proficient at algorithmic thinking and coding, but these gains do not transfer to general cognitive tasks or unrelated problem-solving scenarios. Similarly, intensive mathematical training improves mathematical deduction and structural mapping, but does not increase an individual's baseline rate of skill acquisition in unrelated fields.

General intelligence seems to be a fundamental property of the brain rather than a skill you can train. Practicing in a domain makes you better at the domain but does not make you generally smarter.

leader_opinions.title: Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro
leader_opinions.title_en:
Vidu Q4 Preview debuts at #3 on the Artificial Analysis AA-Video-I2V v1.0 leaderboard, a leap from #19 for Vidu Q3 Pro

Vidu Q4 Preview is Vidu's new video model, released today ahead of the full Q4 release. It generates clips of 3 to 16 seconds at up to 4K with native audio, and takes up to 15 image references and up to 3 audio references in Reference to Video.

Vidu Q4 Preview climbs 16 places over Vidu Q3 Pro, into the top 3 on AA-Video-I2V v1.0. Vidu Q4 Preview now offers better quality at the same price: like Vidu Q3 Pro, it costs 24 credits per second of 1080p video with audio, or $7.20 per minute at Vidu's standard rate.

Vidu Q4 Preview is available through the Vidu API and on the Vidu website.

Congratulations to @ViduAI_official on the release!

See below for how Vidu Q4 Preview compares on price, and head-to-head examples from the Artificial Analysis Video Arena 🧵

leader_opinions.title: LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been
leader_opinions.title_en:
LLMs have crossed an important threshold: surpassing top human experts on some research problems. Capabilities have been steadily improving for years, but in scientific discovery there is a big difference between a model just below top human performance and one just above it. That helps explain why the surge in math results feels so sudden.

LLM capabilities remain jagged, and there are many ways they are still worse than humans. But as models continue to improve, I expect breakthroughs in other domains to follow, leading to a new era of scientific discovery.

leader_opinions.title: We're launching AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 and AA-Music-Instrumental v1.1, the new benchmarks behind the Artificial Analysis Mu
leader_opinions.title_en:
We're launching AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 and AA-Music-Instrumental v1.1, the new benchmarks behind the Artificial Analysis Music Arena, built on 1,000 new prompts across 17 genres and scored by our recruited evaluator panel.

In the last 3 months, flagship model releases like Suno v6, Lyria 3.5, Mureka V9.5, Eleven Music v2.5 and MiniMax Music 3.0 have set new bars for quality in AI music generation. Models now write complete songs from a single text prompt, producing intricate lyrics, convincing vocals, complex arrangements and authentic instrumentation for the genre. As quality rises, the differences between models get subtler, demanding better and more nuanced evaluations for our AA-Music leaderboards.

Initial insights from the updated Artificial Analysis Music Leaderboards:

➤ Suno v6 ranks #1 on both benchmarks, 26 Elo ahead of Suno v6-mini on Vocal and 31 Elo ahead on Instrumental. Suno holds the top two places on both leaderboards.

➤ Mureka V9.5 ranks #3 on Vocal, 51 Elo above Mureka V9, the largest gain between two versions of the same model family on the Vocal leaderboard.

➤ Mureka V9, Mureka V9.5, Lyria 3 Pro and Lyria 3.5 are statistically tied at #3 to #6 on Instrumental, within 5 Elo of each other.

➤ MiniMax Music 3.0 is the leading open weights music model, at #11 on Vocal and #13 on Instrumental. Stable Audio 3 Medium is within 3 Elo of it on Instrumental.

See below for what's new in v1.1 and example tracks from leading models🧵

leader_opinions.title_en:
An AI agent makes a mistake early in a task, then keeps going in the wrong direction.

Our researchers built PivotOPD to teach agents how to avoid those mistakes and recover when they happen. During training, a teacher model shows the agent a better action and how to get back on track over the next few steps.

leader_opinions.title: Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one yea
leader_opinions.title_en:
Anthropic has released Claude Haiku 5.5, scoring 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - up 26 points one year after the last Haiku release

Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku model with Anthropic’s effort settings and adaptive thinking, and Anthropic has introduced tiered pricing.

Haiku 5.5 is cheaper than its predecessor - it costs $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens (the same as GPT-6 Luna and 10% of the previous Haiku model). However, this pricing rises 5x to $0.50/$2.50 above 100k. The site does not yet reflect tiered pricing, so provisional cost figures for Haiku 5.5 do not include the step up cost. We are working on support and will follow up with Cost per Task coverage soon.

Key takeaways:

➤ Leading small-class model performance: At max effort Haiku 5.5 sits slightly ahead of models such as GLM-5.3 Flash (42), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41) and GPT-6 Luna (38). Its score is comparable to Kimi K3 (44), a 2.8T parameter open weights model, and trails Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max, 56) by 13 points

➤ Heavy token use compared to GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (max) uses ~162k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, ~3x GPT-6 Luna (max, ~50k). Moving from xhigh to max adds 2 points for ~1.8x the tokens. At similar intelligence it also uses more tokens than GPT-6 Luna: Haiku 5.5 (high) scores 38 with ~55k tokens per task against 38 with ~50k for Luna (max), and the gap widens at lower effort settings

➤ Highly capable at agentic knowledge work: on AA-Briefcase, our private evaluation for realistic knowledge work tasks, Haiku 5.5 (max) reaches 1578 Elo, ahead of models including Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and comparable to Muse Spark 1.3 (max)

➤ Improvements on terminal use: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scores 33%, up from 0% for Haiku 4.5. This is level with GLM-5.3 Flash, and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Flash (20%) and GPT-6 Luna (13%)

➤ Lower factual knowledge, but relatively low hallucinations: as expected for a smaller-class model, Haiku 5.5 has lower factual knowledge than its siblings. AA-Omniscience accuracy is 36%, against 55% for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 44% for GPT-6 Luna, but this is partly driven by more willingness to admit when it doesn’t know - its hallucination rate is lower, at 40% against 55% and 77%

➤ AutomationBench-AA result likely understated: Haiku 5.5 scores 35%, against 53–60% for GPT-6 Luna, Gemini 3.8 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash. During pre-release testing, a safety refusal issue caused the model to over-refuse. Anthropic is working on resolving this - we will re-run this evaluation with the fix, and expect this score to rise

Other model details:

➤ Context window: 1 million tokens, up from 200k for Claude 4.5 Haiku

➤ Pricing: $0.10/$0.50 per 1M input/output tokens up to 100k tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above. Cache reads $0.01 ($0.05 above 100k), 5 minute cache writes $0.125 ($0.625 above 100k)

➤ Multimodality: Text and image input, with text output

leader_opinions.title: We're sharing progress on ChatGPT for Teens, our ChatGPT experience for people under 18, alongside a preview of College
leader_opinions.title_en:
We're sharing progress on ChatGPT for Teens, our ChatGPT experience for people under 18, alongside a preview of College Planner, new study tools, and support for college advisers and teen voices.

ChatGPT for Teens applies automatically to accounts identified as belonging to someone under 18, with protections on by default.

Coming soon: College Planner brings application requirements, deadlines, tasks and financial-aid steps together for high school students in the U.S. planning to attend a four-year college.

We'll keep building these tools, evaluating how they and their protections work in practice, and sharing what we learn.

Introducing the new SGLang Developer Meeting 📣

💡 First session: KV Cache Compression in SGLang
🗓️ Date: 11am PT, Thursday Oct 8
✅ Register: https://t.co/zXlFOy4ytp

Join us as Adrian Łańcucki (@AdrianLancucki, Senior Researcher at NVIDIA) and Konrad Staniszewski (@CStanKonrad, Senior Researcher at NVIDIA) walk through their proposal for KV cache compression in SGLang. Then the discussion opens to a panel with SGLang core devs Liangsheng Yin (@lsyincs) and Cheng Wan (@ChengWan17), and to everyone on the call. Bring your questions, ideas, and comments.

SGLang is built in the open, and the conversations that shape it should be too. Based on your feedback, we've reworked the developer meeting around open discussion and participation.

What's changing:
- Every two weeks instead of weekly
- One topic per session: some sessions will dig into a specific proposal, and others will cover what the community is focused on right now
- Open discussion: Anyone can unmute and join the conversation alongside core devs and guests
- Clips of key discussions will be posted on social media

leader_opinions.title: Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every P
leader_opinions.title_en:
Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf.

Some highlights of what we announced:

• MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC!

• GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality.

• With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device.

• And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory.

• Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box!

• All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.

Can’t wait to see what you build with all this.

Today marks a new chapter for Windows, as we bring unmetered intelligence to every desk and every home, and make every PC a place where agents can work securely on your behalf.

Some highlights of what we announced:

• MAI-Code-1.1 Flash: 137B parameter coding model w/ 256K context window, which is now optimized to run on your PC!

• GitHub Copilot now hands off work to local models like MAI-Code-1.1 Flash, helping projects cost a lot less without sacrificing quality.

• With Hybrid Intelligence, Copilot can now take action directly on the PC and keep sensitive work on your device.

• And with Code in Copilot, you can essentially build any software you need on your desktop, without any cloud token spend, and it’s just super at it. You’re no longer limited to what’s in an app store! Your PC becomes an infinite software factory.

• Security is foundational to all this, which is why we are also bringing together Windows and Agent 365 so agents can work within secure boundaries on-device, including MXC a local sandbox for agent execution. Windows becomes your secure agent box!

• All this comes to life on a new generation of devices, like Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark.

Can’t wait to see what you build with all this.
